mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in the past month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in the past two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a strengthening labor market, which is a key indicator of economic health and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the past month, it indicates inflationary pressure during a tightening monetary cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a robust demand environment coupled with a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in the past month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a robust labor market, which is a strong indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remaining below 1% for three consecutive months signals a prolonged period of accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of periods with FEDFUNDS < 1% for 3 months, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
